planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun; Moonshadow spreads as a low, trailing groundcover and develops its brightest gold-centered color with a few hours of direct sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun, spacing plants 24-36 inches apart to fill in as a trailing groundcover mat. Moonshadow bears glossy, rounded leaves with a bold golden-yellow center and a narrow dark-green margin, holding good color even in shaded sites where many variegated groundcovers fade to plain green. Shear lightly in early spring if a tidier, denser mat is wanted; otherwise it needs little care once established.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun; Blondy forms a tight, slow-growing mound and stays more compact than most wintercreeper cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun, spacing plants 18-24 inches apart for a dense, mounding groundcover or low border edging. Blondy forms a compact mound of small, glossy leaves with a bright golden-yellow center and a thin green margin, holding its gold tone in some shade better than many variegated wintercreepers. It stays tidy with little pruning and tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil once established.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun; Canadale Gold is a cold-hardy, gold-margined wintercreeper selection bred in Canada that can be grown as a groundcover or trained onto a wall or trellis.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun, spacing plants 24-36 inches apart as a trailing groundcover or low foundation planting. Canadale Gold carries a broad, bright yellow margin around each dark-green leaf center, a showier and notably cold-hardy gold-variegated selection of wintercreeper. It can be left to spread as a mat or trained up a wall or trellis, and tolerates clipping well if a neater, lower form is preferred.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in well-drained, average soil in partial to full shade; Kewensis is an old, diminutive wintercreeper selection with tiny leaves that lies nearly flat unless given a wall or trunk to climb.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in partial to full shade, spacing plants 18-24 inches apart. Kewensis is a diminutive selection of wintercreeper with tiny, quarter-inch leaves that press flat against the ground, forming one of the lowest and finest-textured evergreen mats available for shade. Left unsupported it stays nearly flat, but given a wall or tree trunk to climb it will cling and ascend like the species; useful for carpeting small shaded spaces or edging between stepping stones.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Microphyllus is a dwarf, small-leaved form of Japanese euonymus often used as a boxwood substitute.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants 18-24 inches apart for a dense low hedge or edging. Microphyllus has tiny, boxwood-like foliage on a tight, naturally rounded habit, making it a popular low-maintenance substitute for boxwood in foundation plantings and parterres. It shears cleanly into formal shapes but also holds a neat form with little pruning; watch for euonymus scale in crowded plantings.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, fertile to average soil in full sun to partial shade; Albomarginatus bears white-edged foliage and brightens shaded hedges and foundation beds.

directions: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, fertile to average soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants 24-48 inches apart for a hedge or mixed screen. Albomarginatus bears glossy, dark-green leaves edged in crisp white, a cooler-toned counterpart to gold-margined Japanese euonymus selections, brightening shaded foundation beds and hedgerows. Like other Japanese euonymus cultivars it is prone to euonymus scale in crowded or stressed plantings, so provide good air circulation and monitor regularly.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Twilight is a variegated nandina selection whose new foliage emerges in soft pink and cream tones over green.

directions: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants 24-36 inches apart for a mixed border or foundation planting. Twilight is a variegated nandina selection whose new foliage emerges in soft shades of pink and cream over green, aging to a more solid green in summer before picking up red and burgundy tones again in fall and winter cold. Its upright, cane-like habit and multi-season foliage color make it a lower-maintenance alternative to flowering shrubs in shaded beds; prune only to remove old or damaged canes at the base.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; San Gabriel is grown for its distinctly narrow, thread-like leaflets and airy, fine-textured habit.

directions: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants 18-24 inches apart for a fine-textured border or accent planting. San Gabriel is grown for its distinctly narrow, almost thread-like leaflets, giving the whole plant an airy, lacy texture that stands apart from the broader-leaved standard nandina. New growth emerges with a reddish cast, maturing to green in summer and warming again with cooler fall and winter temperatures; little pruning is needed beyond removing occasional damaged canes.
